shadows.name: none

shadows.name: click-halo

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Border-weight and tint changes on hover and focus. No transforms — nothing lifts.

narrative.overview:
ClickerG blocks traffic silently inside someone else’s ad platform. The advertiser never sees the product work — they see traffic disappear and are asked to believe it was the right traffic. Every other way of answering that question describes behaviour: a bot probability, a scroll percentage, a dwell time. This system shows it instead. The primary object on screen is a wireframe of the page the visitor actually landed on, with what they did drawn onto it — how far down they got, where the mouse went, where they clicked, and, most importantly, where none of that happened.

That last part is the whole argument. A click farm’s replay is a page with a two-percent shaded band, no mouse line anywhere, and a bordered marker in the middle reading no mouse movement recorded. An advertiser does not need the bot probability explained to them; they can see that nobody was there.

The surface is deliberately plain: near-white, one hairline, no shadow, no radius. This is not a minimalist preference, it is deference. Everything decorative competes with a picture whose job is to be believed.
keyCharacteristics: The page replay is the evidence, not an illustration beside it
Absence is drawn explicitly — a bordered marker, never a blank space or a dash
Blue means behaviour was recorded; red means it was not. Nothing else carries either colour
Flat by construction: no radius, no shadow, one hairline border
Manrope for everything read, Fira Code for everything measured
The picture leads, the numbers follow, the prose comes last

rules.name: The Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: Blue means behaviour was recorded. Red means it was not. A third hue, or either of these two used for anything else, breaks the only colour language this system has.

rules.name: The Graphic-and-Text Split Rule
rules.body: #3b82f6 is legible as a graphic at 3.16:1 but fails as text. Keep it on the scroll band and the mouse path; switch to #0b5fe9 the moment the blue becomes type.

rules.name: The Low-Contrast Wireframe Rule
rules.body: The wireframe greys must stay quiet enough that drawn behaviour reads on top of them.

rules.name: The Measured-in-Mono Rule
rules.body: If it is a quantity it is Fira Code. If it is language it is Manrope. There is no third case.

rules.name: The Ten-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing renders below 10px, markers included. If a marker will not fit at 10px it belongs in the caption beneath the frame.

rules.name: The Strip-Scrolls-Not-Wraps Rule
rules.body: The per-arrival strip scrolls horizontally and never wraps. Comparing arrivals side by side is the argument; stacking them destroys it.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separating, move it a step on the ground/frame/surface scale or give it a hairline. The click halo is the only shadow and it is a mark, not elevation.

rules.name: The Border-Weight-Is-Status Rule
rules.body: A blocked card takes a 2px ink border; a decisive arrival takes 2px absence red. Status is carried by border weight and the tag, never by tinting a whole surface.

rules.name: The One Curve Rule
rules.body: If it is not a click, it is not round.

rules.name: The Absence-Is-Drawn Rule
rules.body: When a signal was not recorded, the replay says so in a bordered marker placed where the behaviour would have been. Never a blank frame, never a dash, never an omission.

rules.name: The Marks-Must-Be-Real Rule
rules.body: Everything drawn on a replay must come from recorded data. The scroll band, the no-mouse marker and the click count are backed today. A mouse path and click positions are not. Until the tag records coordinates, draw only what is real and let absence carry the argument.

dos: Do let the replay lead. The picture is the evidence; the numbers support it.
Do draw absence explicitly, in a bordered marker, where the behaviour would have been.
Do keep blue for recorded behaviour and red for its absence — and switch blue to #0b5fe9 the moment it becomes text.
Do set every quantity in Fira Code and every piece of language in Manrope.
Do separate surfaces with the ground/frame/surface scale and a hairline.
Do let the arrival strip scroll sideways rather than wrap.
Do verify any new colour against the composited background, not the raw token.
donts: Don’t draw a mouse path or a click position that is not in the data. Say it is not recorded.
Don’t add a shadow or a radius. The click dot and its halo are the only exceptions.
Don’t introduce a third hue, or spend blue or red on anything but their one meaning.
Don’t render text below 10px, markers included.
Don’t darken the wireframe greys until they compete with the behaviour drawn on top.
Don’t let the replay become decoration beside a table.
Don’t wrap or stack the per-arrival strip — the side-by-side comparison is the finding.
